verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents an HTTP API for sending data from your backend. It also documents delivery-durability mechanisms: Kafka buffering while the warehouse is offline, deduplication of resent data, and a dead-letter queue whose failed events can be replayed. The pack contains no evidence of how ingestion requests are authenticated, such as write keys or tokens; the API-token and OAuth items cover management and MCP access, not ingestion. Missing for 10: documented authentication for the HTTP ingestion API, endpoint/payload reference depth, independent hands-on corroboration of server-side ingestion and delivery guarantees.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can send events server-to-server through a documented HTTP ingestion API with authentication and delivery guarantees

citations.quote: You can use HTTP API to send data to Jitsu. This is useful if you want to send data from your backend.
Jitsu will keep your data in a Kafka and deliver it once the warehouse is back online
Send same data as many times as you want. Jitsu will deduplicate it for you
Dead-letter queue with a reprocessing worker: failed events can be replayed instead of lost.
